content.title: About
content.content: Danish pastry with fruit is a layered dessert made from a yeasted, butter‑rich dough and a variety of berry or fruit fillings. The dough is repeatedly folded to create light, crisp layers, while the fruit adds a sweet‑tart flavor and aromatic notes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The tradition of Danish pastry originated in Europe in the 19th century and quickly spread worldwide.
Fruit fillings may include cherry, blueberry, strawberry, apple or apricot, depending on the season.
The laminated dough requires a specific technique of rolling and folding to achieve the characteristic layers.
Denmark celebrates “Pastry Tuesday,” when cafés serve a range of Danish buns, including fruit‑filled versions.
A hint of vanilla extract is said to enhance the buttery aroma of the pastry.

items.title: Rich source of energy
items.content: The layered dough provides carbohydrates that quickly supply the body with energy.

items.title: Vitamins and antioxidants
items.content: Fruit fillings deliver vitamin C, vitamin A and polyphenols that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Calcium and magnesium
items.content: Butter and whole‑grain flour in the dough contain minerals that support bone and muscle health.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fruit pieces add fiber, promoting healthy digestion.

items.title: Small amount of protein
items.content: Eggs used in the dough provide a modest amount of animal protein.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Fruit syrup and added sugar can increase calories and affect blood glucose levels.

items.title: Gluten and dairy allergies
items.content: The dough contains wheat and butter, which may be problematic for people with celiac disease or lactose intolerance.

items.title: Trans fats from improper preparation
items.content: Using margarine instead of butter can introduce trans fats into the pastry.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The buttery layers make the pastry energy‑dense, so portion control is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Danish pastry with fruit can be enjoyed as a dessert with tea or coffee, cut into bite‑size pieces and served with a light whipped cream. It also pairs well with ice cream or yogurt.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the pastry in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage, keep it in the refrigerator, where it stays fresh for up to 5 days. Reheat in the oven for 5‑10 minutes before serving to restore the crisp layers.
